Table: NGVS Core Region Galaxies: Photometric Parameters

Byte-by-byte Description of file: apjab339ft5_mrt.txt
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Bytes Format Units        Label    Explanations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1- 27 A27    ---          NGVS     NGVS identifier
      29 I1     ---          Class    Membership class code (1)
  31- 35 F5.2   mag          gmagCG   Curve of Growth total g band magnitude (2)
  37- 40 F4.1   ---          C80/20   ? Curve of Growth concentration (3) 
  42- 46 F5.1   arcsec       reCG     Curve of Growth effective radius  
  48- 52 F5.2   mag/arcsec2  mue      Curve of Growth surface brightness 
                                       at reCG (2)
  54- 58 F5.2   mag/arcsec2  <mue>    Median Curve of Growth surface brightness
                                       within reCG (2)
  60- 64 F5.2   mag/arcsec2  mu0      Curve of Growth surface brightness at
                                       central location (2)
  66- 70 F5.2   arcsec       gmagS    Sersic fit g band magnitude; integrated
                                       to infinity (2)
  72- 74 F3.1   mag/arcsec2  n        Sersic value 
  76- 81 F6.2   ---          reS      Sersic fit effective radius
  83- 87 F5.2   mag/arcsec2  mueS     Sersic fit effective surface brightness
                                       at reS (2)
  89- 93 F5.2   mag/arcsec2  <mueS>   Median Sersic fit effective surface
                                       brightness with reS (2)
  95- 95 I1     ---          NucID    Nuclear identifier (4)
  96- 96 A1     ---        u_NucID    [:] Uncertainty flag on NucID
  98-102 F5.2   mag          gmagNuc  ? Sersic fit g band nucleus magnitude (5)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Note (1): See Section 3.1.
    0 = certain member;
    1 = likely member;
    2 = possible member.
Note (2): Magnitudes and surface brightnesses are not corrected for 
          Galactic extinction.
Note (3): Defined as the ratio between the radii containing 80% and 20% 
          of the total light.
Note (4): 
    0 = non-nucleated galaxies (Sersic fit);
    1 = nucleated galaxies (double Sersic fit);
    2 = galaxies with a nucleus offset from the center of the 
        isophotes (double Sersic fit).
        For nucleated galaxies, the Sersic index refers to the model best 
        fitting the main body of the galaxy, but gmagS, reS, mueS, and <mueS>
        account for both components.
Note (5): When it can be reliably derived from the parametric fits.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
